title: SAML in-flight provisioning and step-up handshake: reauth windows, audit hooks, and admin controls
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current SAML session model doesn't preserve strong admin and compliance guarantees during in-flight JIT provisioning and step-up MFA handshakes. Edge cases observed: delayed group sync means RBAC v2 role mapping can be inconsistent during reauth; logout propagation races with JIT user creation; audit logs lack context tying a step-up event to the original inbound SAML assertion and admin policy decisions.

Goal: Define and implement a deterministic in-flight provisioning and step-up handshake flow that: preserves RBAC v2 mapping correctness during reauth; provides explicit grace/retry semantics for JIT provisioning; produces enriched audit events linking assertion IDs, AAD/IdP session IDs, and admin policy triggers; and exposes admin controls (force revoke, grace extension, bypass rules) with clear SLOs for failure modes.

Scope: session token lifecycle changes, SAML assertion binding during JIT creation, reauth window policy, step-up MFA expectations, logout coordination across multi-region sessions, audit schema extension, and Console admin controls for emergency session management. Not in scope: upstream IdP behavior changes, long-term RBAC policy language revamp (we'll use existing RBAC v2 constructs).
updates: 2025-09-15 — Ticket created after incident where admin-initiated revoke did not remove a session created by JIT provisioning in another region. Added initial problem statement and goals.

2025-09-16 — Spike completed: validated approach to bind SAML assertion ID and IdP session ID to our short-lived access token and KV entry; prototype adds 64-bit assertion fingerprint to token claims.

2025-09-17 — Design review with PM and Security: agreed on 3s canonical binding window for in-flight JIT to avoid races, and 2-step rollback if group-sync fails (soft-role followed by hard-role after successful sync).

2025-09-18 — Engineering notes: implemented audit event schema draft (fields: assertion_fingerprint, idp_session_id, stepup_trigger, admin_action, original_request_ts) and added to runtime audit sink. Sending to observability for sample retention planning.

2025-09-19 — Security review in progress: requested clarifications around token binding rotation and KMS involvement. Minor changes to ensure assertion_fingerprint is hashed before persistence to S3 logs.

2025-09-20 — UX/Console: added wireframe for 'Active SAML Sessions' view showing original IdP session, JIT status, last role mapping, and admin revoke button. Planning canary rollout to dedicated tenants.
Open: finalize migration plan for existing long-lived sessions; coordinate with telemetry to flag prior sessions without assertion_fingerprint for 30 days.
proposed_approach: 1) Canonical binding: when a SAML assertion triggers JIT provisioning, persist a hashed assertion_fingerprint and idp_session_id into the session record and KV cache bucket atomically with session creation. This lets subsequent reauth/step-up requests correlate to the exact inbound assertion.

2) Reauth windows: introduce 'reauth_window' policy (default 10 minutes) during which RBAC v2 role mapping is tolerated in a soft-mode if group sync lags. Soft-mode grants limited default scopes until full group mapping completes; after 'reauth_window' expires, re-evaluate roles and either elevate or revoke session accordingly.

3) Step-up handshake: for MFA-required routes, record a 'stepup_trigger' in the audit event and require the client to present an assertion_fingerprint or idp_session_id to avoid replay. Step-up tokens are short-lived (30s) and single-use, bound to the existing session id and assertion_fingerprint.

4) Logout coordination: treat admin logout as a high-priority event that invalidates the local token immediately and publishes a region-wide invalidate message. For sessions in JIT-creation race, we accept idempotent revoke — if the session creation completes after revoke, the bind-check will detect a revoked assertion_fingerprint and immediately expire the session.

5) Audit logging: extend existing audit schema with explicit fields for SAML flows (assertion_fingerprint, assertion_hash_alg, idp_session_id, issuance_ts, synced_groups_version, stepup_trigger, admin_actor). All fields hashed/encrypted as required by compliance.

6) Admin controls: Console exposes 'extend grace', 'force revoke', and 're-run mapping' actions for SAML sessions; each action emits audit events and has a clear SLO (extend/retry within 500ms, force revoke <1s global propagation target).
testing_plan: Unit tests for assertion_fingerprint generation and hashing: collision checks and verifying hash algorithm parameters.
Integration tests: simulate IdP slow group sync to validate soft-mode grant semantics and final reconciliation outcomes.
Chaos/Concurrency tests: create cross-region race between revoke and JIT create to ensure idempotence and immediate invalidation post-creation.
Security tests: ensure assertion_fingerprint isn't reversible; pen-test on step-up token replay and token-binding enforcement.
E2E canary: roll out to 5 dedicated customers with low customer impact window, monitor audit logs, session churn, and reauth error rate.
rollout_plan: Alpha on staging with synthetic IdPs (2025-09-22), alpha observability dashboards enabled.
Beta to canary tenants (2025-09-29): enable only for tenants with SAML enabled and opt-in console toggle.
Full rollout (2025-10-12): after 2-week canary and security sign-off; provide migration tool for legacy sessions to tag assertion_fingerprint where possible.
Post-rollout: telemetry queries to measure reauth_window-related revocations and step-up failure rate for 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: Assertion_fingerprint is emitted and persisted for all JIT provisioning events and present in audit logs for >=95% of new SAML sessions.
Soft-mode reauth grants do not permit admin-scoped actions; RBAC v2 evaluation path correctly upgrades permissions after group sync within reauth_window in >99% of tests.
Admin force-revoke immediately invalidates sessions in <1s for 95th percentile in test clusters and subsequent JIT creations do not rehydrate revoked sessions.
Audit schema changes stored in central audit sink and accessible in console UI; security review sign-off obtained and sensitive fields are hashed before persistence.
No increase in step-up failure rate above baseline after canary (<=0.5% delta) and detailed rollout playbook recorded.
open_questions: What is the canonical TTL for assertion_fingerprint retention in audit logs for compliance? (Security suggests 90 days hashed, Legal may request 365.)
Do we need to involve KMS to sign assertion_fingerprint in addition to hashing for replay protection?
Should soft-mode mapping be configurable per-tenant or enforced globally for safety?
How to surface a clear user-facing error when a step-up handshake fails due to group-sync inconsistency?
